newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria PSK to be turned into joint stock company.
newsitem.headline: Austria PSK to be turned into joint stock company.

text.p: Austria's postal savings bank PSK will be turned into a joint stock company on Wednesday to prepare it for partial privatisation later this year, PSK chief executive Erich Hampel said on Tuesday.
"The base capital will amount to 1.762 billion schillings," Hampel told a news briefing. Hampel was named last week to take over as chief executive of Creditanstalt on May 15.

PSK's entire share capital will be held by holding company PTBG, which is owned by the Austrian government's industrial holding company OeIAG. PTBG also owns the state postal and telecoms monopoly PTA, which is due for privatisation in 1999.
Austria's Bank fuer Arbeit und Wirtschaft, GiroCredit Bank, the Raiffeisen banking group and PTA have signalled interest in taking on up to 49 percent of PSK's capital.

PSK's 1996 net profit fell to 928.8 million schillings from 1.044 billion the previous year, while operating profit eased to 1.7 billion schillings from 1.82 billion. First-quarter operating profit rose to 497 million schillings from 397 million, Hampel said.
The bank's total assets stood at 257.88 billion schillings at year-end, up from 253.43 billion a year earlier.
